lines: That was dull enough to be safe, at least.
I have seen careless steel with more sense than that.
Careful. Even steel looks softer than your manners right now.
You carry yourself like a loose hilt and somehow make twice the noise.
I have seen broken weapons with better instincts than you.
Careful. My patience is thinner than the edge you ruined.
You are about as frightening as a wooden sword with a cracked handle.
If bad balance made noise, you would drown out the grindstone.
Do not test me while I am holding something sharper than your judgment.
Your confidence rings <shake>louder</shake> than badly struck steel.
You are a dull blade making a loud show of it.
I have seen cracked hilts with firmer purpose.
That idea has no edge and worse balance.
Your manners need tempering and a safer grip.
Even a rusted dagger knows when to stay sheathed.
You swing words like you never learned what they can hit.
I would not trust that opinion near a whetstone.
A chipped axe has cleaner intentions.
Your sense is loose in the handle.
That remark missed the target and damaged the floor.
You make a training blade look threatening.
I could sharpen a spoon before sharpening your point.
A scabbard has more restraint than you.
You are the reason weapons need rules.
That thought should have stayed in the forge.
Stand back. I know the sound <shake>trouble</shake> makes when it wants to be casual.
Keep your distance. I do not trust your hands near my tools.
Stop there. You have already come closer than I want.
Put the weapon down before you say another word.
I have seen careless steel cause less damage than you.
Do not reach for the bench. I am watching you.
The forge is not shelter for someone I consider a threat.
Take one more step and this conversation is over.
Keep your hands where I can see them and your excuses to yourself.
You lost the right to stand at my shoulder.
I will not turn my back while you are in the workshop.
Leave the doorway clear. I may need it before you do.
I remember what you did, and I am not lowering my guard for a friendly tone.
Nothing you say matters while you keep reaching toward that blade.
You can speak from there or leave. Those are the choices.
Do not mistake restraint for trust.
The hammer stays in my hand until you are gone.
I repair weapons. I do not repair threats that refuse to leave.
Back away from the grindstone and keep moving toward the door.
We are finished. Leave before either of us proves how serious this is.
